questions.q: A $12V$ battery connected to a coil of resistance $6 Ω$ through a switch, drives a constant current in the circuit. The switch is opened in $1$ ms. The emf induced across the coil is $20V$. The inductance of the coil is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The current& \left(i\right)$~through the circuit is given by

$\begin{cases}i & = & \dfrac{V}{R} \\ & = & \dfrac{12V}{6Ω} \\ & = & 2A\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the induced emf in the coil can be written as

$ε = L\dfrac{di}{dt} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the inductance of the coil.

\begin{cases}$20V & = & L \times $\dfrac{2A}{1 \times {10}^{- 3}s}$\\ & ⇒ & L = $\dfrac{20V \times 1 \times {10}^{- 3}s}{2A}$\\ & = & 10mH\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A $10m$ long horizontal wire extends from North East to South West. It is falling with a speed of $5.0ms^{- 1},$ at right angles to the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field of $0.3 \times {10}^{- 4}Wbm^{- 2} .$ The value of the induced emf in the wire is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The wire makes an angle& $45 °$~with the magnetic field lines. Therefore, the induced emf will be,

$ε = Bvlsin{45}^{0}$

$= 0.3 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 5 \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$= 1.1 \times {10}^{- 3}V$

questions.q:
An inductor coil stores $64J$ of magnetic field energy and dissipates energy at the rate of $640W$ when a current of $8A$ is passed through it. If this coil is joined across an ideal battery, find the time constant of the circuit (in $s$).
&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy stored in an inductor,& $U = \dfrac{1}{2}LI^{2}$
$⇒ 64 = \dfrac{1}{2}L ( 8{)}^{2} ⇒ L = 2H$
and power dissipated in a resistor,~$P = I^{2}R$
$⇒ 640 = ( 8{)}^{2}R ⇒ R = 10Ω$
Time constant of the~$LRDC$~circuit is,
$τ = \dfrac{L}{R} = \dfrac{2}{10} = 0 . 2s$

questions.q:
The source of time varying magnetic field may be

(A) a permanent magnet

(B) an electric field changing linearly with time

(C) direct current

(D) a decelerating charge particle

(E) an antenna fed with a digital signal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
An electric field varying linearly with time will not produce variable magnetic field as current will be constant.

A decelerating charged particle can result in a time& varying magnetic field by emitting radiation.

Similarly a permanent magnet has a constant magnetic field and a direct current does not change its direction and cannot produce a magnetic field.

An antenna can modulate the digital signals .

So, the right option is the statement D.

questions.q: A $20$~$\text{H}$ inductor coil is connected to a $10Ω$& resistance in series as shown in figure. The time at which rate of dissipation of energy& (Joule's heat)& across resistance is equal to the rate at which magnetic energy is stored in the inductor, is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Rate of dissipation of energy in resistor $= i^{2}R$
Rate of energy stored in inductor $= \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}Li^{2}\right) = Li\dfrac{di}{dt}$
$i^{2}R = Li\dfrac{di}{dt}$
$\dfrac{di}{dt} = i\dfrac{R}{L} \ldots \left(i\right)$
In $L - R$ circuit:

$i = {i}_{0}\left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{t}{τ}}\right) ( ∴ τ = $\dfrac{L}{R} =$2 )$
\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{{i}_{0}}{τ}$e^{- t / τ}$
From equation (i),

\dfrac{{i}_{0}}{τ}$e^{- t / τ} = {i}_{0}\left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{t}{τ}}\$right)\dfrac{R}{L}
$e^{- t / τ} = 1 - e^{- t / τ}$
$e^{- $\dfrac{t}{τ}} = $\dfrac{1}{2}$⇒ t = τln2$
$= 2ln2$

$

questions.q:
A small square loop of wire of side $l$~is placed inside a large square loop of wire $L \left(L ≫ l\right)$. Both loops are coplanar and their centres coincide at point $O as shown in figure. The mutual inductance of the system is

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

Let a current,& $I$ pass through the square loop of side,~$L$. The magnetic field at the centre $O$,

$B = 4 \times Magneticfieldduetoeach side$

$⇒ B = 4 \times \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} ⋅ \dfrac{I}{L / 2} \left(sin{45}^{∘} + sin{45}^{∘}\right)$

$⇒ B = $\dfrac{2{μ}_{0}I}{\piL}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}{μ}_{0}I}{\piL}

Magnetic flux linked with the small square loop,

$ϕ = BA = Bl^{2} = $\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}{μ}_{0}Il^{2}}{\piL}

Mutual inductance of the coil,~

$M = \dfrac{ϕ}{I} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}{μ}_{0}l^{2}}{\piL}.$

$

questions.q: A coil is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of $5000T$. When the field is changed to $3000T$ in $2s$, an induced emf of $22V$ is produced in the coil. If the diameter of the coil is $0 . 02m$, then the number of turns in the coil is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Average induced EMF is given by, $ε = N \left(\dfrac{∆ ϕ}{t}\right)

Also, change in flux $∆ ϕ = ( ∆ B ) A$

Given: ${B}_{i} = 5000T$,

${B}_{f} = 3000T$

$d = 0 . 02m ⇒ r = $\dfrac{d}{2} =$0 . 01m$

Hence,

$∆ ϕ = ( ∆ B ) A$

$= \left($2000\right)$\pi\left($0 . 01\right)2 = 0 . 2$\pi

EMF, $ε = N \left(\dfrac{∆ ϕ}{t}\right) ⇒ 22 = N \left(\dfrac{0 . 2\pi}{2}\right)

$⇒ N = 70$

$

questions.q: For the plane electromagnetic wave given by $E = {E}_{0}sin ( \omegat – kx )$~and $B = {B}_{0}sin ( \omegat - kx ) ,$& the& ratio of average electric energy density to average magnetic energy density is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the average electric energy density is given by

${U}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} . . . ( 1 )$

and, the formula to calculate average magnetic energy density is given by

${U}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2{μ}_{0}}B^{2} . . . ( 2 )$

For any particular electromagnetic wave,~both magnetic and electric field are equally involved in contributing to energy density. Hence, the ratio of average electric~energy density to magnetic energy density is~$1$.

questions.q:
In the circuit shown,

the switch $S_{1}$ is closed at time $t=0$ and the switch $S_{2}$ is kept open. At some later time \left(\mathrm{t}_{0}\right)$, the switch $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ is opened and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ is closed. the behaviour of the current I as a function of time ' $\mathrm{t}$ ' is given by:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The current will grow for the time $\mathrm{t}=0$ to $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{t}_{0}$ and after that decay of current takes place.
Growth and decay of current is of exponential nature
$\mathrm{i}=\mathrm{i}_0\left(1-\mathrme^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{\tau}}\right) \rightarrow \text { during growth }$
$\mathrm{i}=\mathrm{i}_{\max } \mathrme^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{\tau}} \rightarrow \text { during decay }$

questions.q:
Regarding self-inductance:
A. The self-inductance of the coil depends on its geometry.
B. Self-inductance does not depend on the permeability of the medium.
C. Self-induced e.m.f. opposes any change in the current in a circuit.
D. Self-inductance is electromagnetic analogue of mass in mechanics.
E. Work needs to be done against self-induced e.m.f. in establishing the current. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: A. The self-inductance of the coil depends on its geometry. This is true because the self-inductance of a coil is given by formulas that include its geometrical parameters (number of turns, cross-sectional area, length, etc.). For example, for a solenoid, \(L=\mu_0 \mu_r $\frac{N^2 A}{l}$\) where \(N\) is the number of turns, \(A\) is the cross-sectional area, and \(l\) is the length. B. Self-inductance does not depend on the permeability of the medium. This is false. The permeability of the medium (represented by \(\mu=\mu_0 \mu_r\)) directly influences the inductance, as seen in the formula above. So, any change in the medium's permeability will affect the inductance. C. Self-induced e.m.f. opposes any change in the current in a circuit. This is true, and it is a direct consequence of Lenz's law. The induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) always acts in a direction such that it opposes the change in current that produced it. D. Self-inductance is the electromagnetic analogue of mass in mechanics. This is true. Just as mass resists changes in velocity (inertia), inductance resists changes in current, which is why it is often compared to the inertial mass in mechanical systems. E. Work needs to be done against self-induced e.m.f. in establishing the current. This is true because, when you try to change the current, you must do work to overcome the opposing self-induced e.m.f., storing energy in the magnetic field of the inductor. Based on the above reasoning, the true statements are \($\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}$\), and E. Thus, the correct answer is: Option C A, C, D, E only

questions.q: A coil of self inductance $10mH$ and resistance of $0.1Ω$ is connected through a switch to a battery of internal resistance $0.9Ω$ . After the switch is closed, the time taken for the current to attain $80%$ of the saturation value is:~$[ ln5 = 1.6 ]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$The instantaneous current in an LR circuit is given by the equation :
(instantaneous current)& $I = {I}_{s} \left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{Rt}{L}}\right)$

Where~$I, {I}_{s}, R, t, L$~are the instantaneous current, saturation current, resistance, time and inductance respectively.

Given that the current becomes so percent of saturation current.
$⇒ \left(0.8\right){I}_{s} = {I}_{s} \left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{Rt}{L}}\right)$

$R = 0 . 1\text{Ω} +0 . 9\text{Ω} =1\text{Ω}$
$⇒ 0.8 = \left($1 - e^{- $\dfrac{1 \times t}{10 \times {10}^{- 3}}}\right)$
$⇒ 0.8 = 1 - e^{- 100t}$
Therefore, the time is:
$t = $\dfrac{ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - 0.8}\right)}{100} = \dfrac{ln ⁡ \left(5\right)}{100} =$0.016s$

$

questions.q: Consider the LR circuit shown in the figure. If the switch S is closed at $t = 0$ then the amount of charge that passes through the battery between $t = 0$ and $t = \dfrac{L}{R}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The current in the LR circuit& at any time& $t$ is
$I = \dfrac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{- $\dfrac{Rt}{L}}\right)$

Where~$E, R, L, I$~are the EMF, resistance, inductance and the current respectively.
$∴$ Charge flown through the circuit from time 0 to~\dfrac{L}{R}~is~
(charge)~$∆ q = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{LR}I . dt = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{LR}\d$dfrac{E}{R}\left(1 - e^{- \dfrac{Rt}{L}}\right)dt$
$⇒ ∆ q = \dfrac{E}{R}{t + \dfrac{L}{R}e^{- \dfrac{Rt}{L}}}_{0}^{LR}$
$⇒ ∆ q = \dfrac{E}{R} \left[\dfrac{L}{R} + \dfrac{L}{R}e^{- 1} - \dfrac{L}{R}\right]$
$⇒ ∆ q = \dfrac{E}{R} \times \dfrac{L}{eR}$
$⇒ ∆ q = \dfrac{EL}{eR^{2}} = \dfrac{EL}{2.7R^{2}}$

questions.q:
A metallic rod of length $L$~is rotated with an angular speed of $\omega$~normal to a uniform magnetic field $B$& about an axis passing through one end of rod as shown in figure. The induced emf will be :

.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Linear velocity at the distance $x$~from the centre can be written as,~$v = \omegax$.

Therefore, induced EMF due to small element will be,

$dε = Bvdx = B\left(\omegax\right)dx$

Integrating both sides, we get

$∫ dε = ∫ B\left(\omegax\right)dx$

$⇒ ε = B\omega{∫}_{0}^{L}xdx = \dfrac{B\omegaL^{2}}{2}$

questions.q: The magnetic flux through a coil perpendicular to its plane is varying according to the relation $ϕ =  \left(5t^{3} + 4t^{2} + 2t - 5\right)$ Weber. If the resistance of the coil is $5ohm$, then the induced current through the coil at $t = 2s will be,$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,& $ϕ = 5t^{3} + 4t^{2} + 2t - 5$

Magnitude of induced emf~$ε = \left|\dfrac{d ϕ}{d t}\right| = 15t^{2} + 8t + 2$

At,~$t = 2s$,~$ε = 60 + 16 + 2 = 78V$

Current,~$i = \dfrac{ε}{R} = \dfrac{78}{5} = 15 . 6A$

questions.q: The magnetic flux $ϕ$ (in weber) linked with a closed circuit of resistance $8Ω$ varies with time (in seconds) as $ϕ = 5t^{2} - 36t + 1$. The induced current in the circuit at $t = 2s$ is _______ $A$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Induced EMF is given by, \left|ε\right| = \left|- \left(\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right)\right| = \left|10t - 36\right|$

Now, it is given that at $t = 2s, ε = 16V$.

Therefore, $i = \left|ε\right|R = \dfrac{16}{8} = 2A$

$

questions.q: A $1m$~long metal rod $XY$ completes the circuit as shown in figure. The plane of the circuit is perpendicular to the magnetic field of flux density $0 . 15T$. If the resistance of the circuit is $5 Ω$, the force needed to move the rod in direction, as indicated, with a constant speed of $4ms^{- 1}$ will be _______{10}^{– 3}N.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The force on the rod is given by

$F = ilB$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{Bvl}{R} \times lB$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}v}{R} . . . ( i )$

The data given is

$R = 5Ωl = 1mv = 4ms^{- 1}B = 0 . 15T$

Substituting the values in equation (i)

$F = \dfrac{\left(0 . 15\right)2 \times \left(1\right)2 \times 4}{5}$

$= 18 \times {10}^{- 3}N$

questions.q: A $10Ω, 20mH$ coil carrying constant current is connected to a battery of $20V$ through a switch. Now after switch is opened current becomes zero in $100\mus$. The average e.m.f. induced in the coil is _____~$V$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The initial current in the coil will be,& $i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{20}{10} = 2A$.

Average e.m.f. developed in the coil will be,

$ε = - \dfrac{∆ ϕ}{∆ t} = \dfrac{0 - Li}{t} = \dfrac{20 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 2}{100 \times {10}^{- 6}} = 400V$.
